subject: Clarify: streaming + context-stitching billing and rounding behavior
messages:
From: Sam Ortega <sam.ortega@novahealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Leila Haddad <procurement@novahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 7 May 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Billing for streaming sessions that stitch contexts

Hi Tessa —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement has a few follow ups before we can finalize the SOW. Two technical billing questions came up that the finance team wants written confirmation on:

1) If we stream multiple short calls that are later stitched server-side into a single user conversation (prefix + new input), how are tokens accounted? Are streaming calls billed per-call or merged into a single session bucket when stitched?

2) What rounding rules apply for fractional-token calculations during streaming (partial tokens emitted mid-stream) and when combined into longer contexts? For example, if a streaming call emits 3.4 tokens and next call emits 2.7 but they are stitched into a 6.1 total, do you round per-call or on the stitched total?

Procurement would like a short example and any policy exceptions (pilot credits, minimums) documented so we can map to our internal chargeback model. I attached a sample traffic pattern (billing_math_examples.xlsx).

Appreciate a quick confirmation. We’re hoping to sign by end of next week.

—Sam
Sam Ortega
Head of Platform Integrations
NovaHealth
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Ortega <sam.ortega@novahealth.com>
Cc: Leila Haddad <procurement@novahealth.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 May 2029 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Billing for streaming sessions that stitch contexts

Sam —

Thanks for laying this out and attaching the sheet. Looping in Vanessa and Karthik from pricing/finance to confirm the exact rounding language and any exceptions for pilot accounts. High-level answers below; Vanessa / Karthik please refine with the exact playbook we will include in the SOW.

High-level:
- Stitching: by default Redwood groups requests into "session buckets" when the requests share the same session id / KV prefix and are received within the configured session window (default 30 minutes). When stitched on our side into a single logical conversation, billing is performed on the stitched context (i.e., merged token counts) rather than per ephemeral stream call. This avoids double-charging for prefix reuse.

- Rounding: we round at the invoice-item level after aggregation (post-stitch). That means partial-token emissions from multiple streaming calls are summed and then rounded according to the billing quantum. Our standard quantum is 1 token for metering but we apply a minimum billing floor of 10 tokens for any new interactive session that originates from the hosted API unless a dedicated/reserved capacity contract overrides that.

What I believe this means for your examples: the 3.4 + 2.7 -> 6.1 would be aggregated and billed as 6 tokens (rounded to nearest integer, downward on .4 and upward on .5; see below for rule). If your usage pattern creates many very small sessions we can discuss a pilot concession (partial credits) — Vanessa, can you confirm the concession thresholds?

Vanessa/Karthik — two asks: please confirm the exact rounding tie-breaker (.5 rule) and whether we should call out a different quantum for streaming (some customers prefer a 5-token quantum for high-chat workloads). Also confirm whether the minimum 10-token floor should be explicit in the SOW or handled as a separate billing schedule.

Thanks —
Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Ortega <sam.ortega@novahealth.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Leila Haddad <procurement@novahealth.com>
Date: Wed, 8 May 2029 11:29:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Billing for streaming sessions that stitch contexts

Hi Sam / team —

Thanks for the clear examples — I pulled in the finance playbook and ran the sample sheet. Short answers (policy + worked example):

Policy:
- Aggregation: Redwood aggregates per logical conversation during the invoice window. Logical conversation = same session id + KV prefix linkage within session timeout. Aggregation happens before applying quantum and minimums.
- Quantum & rounding: Metering quantum = 1 token. Aggregation sums fractional tokens across all calls in the conversation, then we apply rounding using "bankers rounding" to reduce bias: fractions of .5 round to the nearest even integer. So 6.5 -> 6 (since 6 is even), 7.5 -> 8.
- Minimums: Hosted API interactive sessions are subject to a 10-token minimum billed per new conversation to account for setup overhead (network + prefix loading). Dedicated/private customers can opt out via contract.
- Pilot credits: For pilot/proof-of-concept customers we can issue a monthly credit that effectively reduces billed tokens for sessions under a configured threshold (we typically set threshold at 1,000 sessions per month with per-session average under 12 tokens). This is negotiable.

Worked example (from your numbers):
- Stream call A: 3.4 tokens
- Stream call B: 2.7 tokens
- Aggregated total = 6.1 tokens -> apply bankers rounding -> 6 tokens billed (no minimum applies because 6 >= 10? actually it is less than 10 so the 10-token minimum applies — see below)
- Apply minimum: since this is a new conversation on hosted API, we invoice at 10 tokens. If the conversation later grows above 10 tokens within the billing window, we bill actual aggregated tokens that exceed the floor; the floor only ensures minimum basis.

Edge behavior to call out in the SOW:
- If you stitch calls client-side and send a single request with full context, the session is billed on the full input/output tokens provided in that single request (no additional session-floor applied if the request is treated as an update to an existing conversation id).
- If prefix reuse is high (your case with a persistent KV across many short calls), we credit prefix tokens once per conversation; KV cache warmup costs are spread across the conversation, not billed per call.

I'll attach a marked-up SOW excerpt and a small table showing how samples map to invoice rows (see attached redwood_terms_v2_markups.pdf and billing_math_examples.xlsx).

If it's helpful, Karthik can provide two SOW language variants: "Hosted standard" and "Hosted with pilot concessions".

-Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Pricing | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Billing for streaming sessions that stitch contexts

Sam / Leila —

Quick follow-up to lock language for the SOW: we propose the following concise clause you can paste into procurement doc. Feel free to redline.

"Billing for stitched conversations: Redwood aggregates metered tokens by logical conversation (same session identifier and linked KV prefix) during the invoice window. Fractional tokens across calls are summed and rounded using bankers rounding (ties to nearest even integer). A minimum bill of 10 tokens per newly created hosted interactive conversation is applied unless otherwise specified in a dedicated capacity or enterprise contract. Pilot customers may receive negotiated monthly credits for low-average sessions; see pricing schedule for thresholds. Prefix/KV reuse credits are applied so customers are not charged repeatedly for identical prefix tokens within the same aggregated conversation."

If that's acceptable we'll add it to the SOW and re-send the redlines. Also happy to set a pilot concession for NovaHealth if you want us to waive the 10-token minimum for the first 90 days.

Thanks —
Karthik
